coaching.summary: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and the bar across your hips, then drive your hips up until shoulders, hips and knees line up.
cues: Rest the bench just under your shoulder blades and pad the bar in the hip crease.
Tuck the chin and keep the ribs down so the hips do the work, not the lower back.
Drive through the heels to full lockout with shins vertical, then lower under control.

introduction.title: Why the Hip Thrust Works So Well
paragraphs: The hip thrust rests your upper back on a bench with a barbell across your hips, then drives the hips up until your shoulders, hips and knees form a straight line. The glutes work hardest right at the top, where the hip is fully extended, which is exactly the point where squats and deadlifts get easiest.
That makes the hip thrust a perfect partner for the big lifts. It builds glute strength and size with very little stress on the lower back, and most lifters can load it heavily within a few months.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between a hip thrust and a glute bridge?
faqItems.answer: A glute bridge is done with your upper back on the floor, which shortens the range of motion. The hip thrust raises your upper back onto a bench, so your hips travel further and usually handle more load.

faqItems.question: How high should the bench be for hip thrusts?
faqItems.answer: A bench around 12 to 16 inches tall suits most people. Your upper back should rest just below the shoulder blades, and at the top of each rep your torso should be roughly parallel to the floor.

faqItems.question: Where should my feet be for a hip thrust?
faqItems.answer: Place them so your shins are vertical at the top of the rep, about hip width apart with the toes turned slightly out. Drive through your heels and keep your knees tracking over your toes.

faqItems.question: Why do I feel hip thrusts in my lower back?
faqItems.answer: Usually the ribs flare and the lower back arches at the top. Tuck your chin, keep your ribs down, and finish each rep by squeezing the glutes rather than lifting the hips higher. A short pause at the top makes the difference easy to feel.

faqItems.question: Do I need a pad for barbell hip thrusts?
faqItems.answer: A bar pad or folded mat makes heavier sets far more comfortable on the hips. It changes nothing about the movement, so use one as soon as the weight starts to press.
